# Introducion (Part 2)

The data used in this CP is the `bloodp` data containing blood pressure measurements from a clinical trial. Familiarize youself with the data by loading the data with `data(bloodp)` and inspecting the data dictionary `?bloodp`.

# Long and wide format

This data set contains all measurements for each patient in a single row (wide format). To analyze the data, these measurements may have to be put into separate rows (long format). Package `reshape2` contains functions to change a data set between long and wide format.

The function `melt` changes from wide into long format.

```{r}
    library('lumc.dabs')
    library('reshape2')
    data(bloodp)
    d <- bloodp
    dLong <- melt(bloodp, c('id', 'group', 'SBP_t1', 'age', 'sex'), c('SBP_t2', 'SBP_t3', 'SBP_t4'), variable.name = 'repeat', value.name = 'sbp')
    # order data set by patient id
    dLong <- dLong[order(dLong$id), ]
    head(dLong)
```

The first argument is the data set in wide format. The second argument are so-called `id.vars`, which identify the units (mice) in the data. Values of these variables are repeated for each measurement in the output data `dLong`. The third argument contains the repeated measurements on the unit (mouse). For each of these columns, a new row is created in the output data per unit. The final arguments determing column names in the output data.

Check `dLong` and make sure you understand how it relates to the original data `d`.

A data set in long format can be converted back to wide format using function `dcast`.

```{r}
    d1 <- dcast(dLong, id + group + age + sex + SBP_t1 ~ `repeat`)
```

This function takes two arguments: the data in long format and a formula of the form `id.vars1 + idvars2 + ... ~ measruement`. The variables on the left hand side are again the identifying variables and the right hand variable is the variable identifying the measurement. The remaining variables are put into separate columns.

Check that `d` and `d1` are identical for the shared columns.

## Q4: Investigate residuals

You can get residuals from your model by using `resid <- lm(sbp ~ ..., dLong)`. Replace your formula in the following code to get the plot:

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.align='center'}
l1 <- lm(sbp ~ group, dLong)
plot(residuals(l1))
```

How do you judge the residuals?
